newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC Pacific seen selling Hongkong Telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pacific seen selling Hongkong Telecom stake.

text.p: Speculation of a deal between Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and a China partner intensified on Friday after trading in Hongkong Telecom shares was halted, with analysts expecting a sale of CITIC Pacific Ltd's holding.
Trading in shares of CITIC Pacific, which holds eight percent of Hongkong Telecom, was also suspended on Friday.
Both China United Telecommunications Corp (China Unicom) and China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPT) have been tipped as possible investors in Hongkong Telecom.
"From what I hear...CITIC (Pacific) is selling down to China Unicom," said an analyst who declined to be named. "China Unicom is injecting a bit of itself into CITIC Pacific."

China Unicom is a joint venture of 16 major Chinese organisations led by the ministries of power, railways and electronics industry. CITIC Pacific's parent, China International Trust and Investment Corp, is one the investors.

CITIC Pacific has already expressed an interest in China's telecoms market, confirming last November it was in talks to invest up to HK$5 billion in mobile phone operator United National Telecommunications Corp.
Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities, said the CITIC Pacific-China Unicom option was possible, but he urged caution.
"There's a lot of different options but it's just pure speculation," he said.
Analysts predicted an announcement sooner rather than later.
"They're not going to suspend two major blue chips for very much longer, so an announcement is obviously going to be imminent," said Rossiter.
Analysts said they had expected to hear something on Thursday when Hongkong Telecom announced its annual profits, but the telecommunications giant remained silent.
"Everyone knows that (Cable and Wireless chief executive) Dick Brown is in town and that adds weight to the rumours that there would be an announcement," said one analyst with a European brokerage.
Cable and Wireless owns 58.5 percent of Hongkong Telecom.
"My personal view is that it (a restructuring of the shareholder base) has to happen now rather than later," said Andrew Fernow, Vickers Ballas research director.
But he added that he was "not that crazy about Unicom".
Analysts said the market was also speculating Cable and Wireless might sell seven percent of Hongkong Telecom and CITIC Pacific might sell its holding into a consortium in which MPT held a stake.
